text: Given the service is running, When the gateway calls tools/list, Then exactly the 9 canva_* tools from Tech design §4 are returned, each description ≤500 chars with a ≤100-char first line.
Given no X-Canva-Access-Token header is sent, When any Canva tool is called, Then the service returns HTTP 401 with a body naming the missing header, not HTTP 500.

Given a valid access token for an account with existing designs, When canva_list_designs is called with no arguments, Then it returns up to 20 designs (id/title/thumbnail_url/edit_url/view_url/updated_at) plus a continuation token if more exist.
steps: Obtain a real Canva Connect access token for a test account that has at least 25 designs (create extra blank designs first if needed, to exercise pagination)
Call canva_list_designs with no arguments against the deployed service
expect: Response contains <=20 designs, each with id/title/thumbnail_url/edit_url/view_url/updated_at populated, and a non-null continuation token (since the account has more than 20 designs)

text: Given Canva returns an empty designs array for a query, When canva_list_designs is called with that query, Then the tool returns an empty list, not an error and not a not_found code.
Given a valid access token and a design id that exists and is visible to that account, When canva_get_design is called, Then it returns id/title/page_count/thumbnail_url/edit_url/view_url.
steps: Using the same test account as TC3, pick one known design id
expect: Response has id, title, page_count >= 1, thumbnail_url, edit_url, view_url, all non-empty

text: Given Canva returns 404 for a design id, When canva_get_design is called with that id, Then the tool returns a structured not_found error, not a raw passthrough of Canva's 4xx body.
Given a valid access token, When canva_create_design is called with a supported design type and a title, Then a new empty design is created in the account and its id + edit_url are returned.
steps: Call canva_create_design(design_type=<a supported preset, e.g. the Instagram Post preset from the design-types endpoint>, title="PRD-21299 smoke test")
Open the returned edit_url in a browser signed in as the same test account
Call canva_list_designs(query="PRD-21299 smoke test") to confirm it is discoverable
expect: Tool returns a new id + edit_url; the edit_url opens a blank design with the given title; the design shows up in canva_list_designs
notes: needs a real vendor account; writes a real design to the test account, clean up afterward

text: Given a valid access token and an existing visible design id, When canva_export_design is called with format=pdf, Then within the internal poll budget it returns download URL(s), or an export_id with status in_progress if the budget runs out — it never hangs past the budget.
steps: Call canva_export_design(design_id=<a single-page test design>, format="pdf")
If status is in_progress, note the export_id for TC9
expect: Response arrives within the documented poll budget (<120s); on success it contains one or more download URLs that resolve to a PDF; on budget exhaustion it returns an export_id and status in_progress, never an unhandled timeout or crash

text: Given an export_id from TC8 that had not finished, When canva_get_export_status is called, Then it returns in_progress and then eventually success with download URL(s) once Canva finishes the job.
steps: Repeat every few seconds until status is success or failed
expect: Status transitions from in_progress to success; once success, the response includes the same shape of download URL(s) as a synchronous export would
notes: needs a real vendor account; only exercised if TC8 did not finish inside its own budget

text: Given a valid access token and a publicly reachable URL to an image, When canva_upload_asset_from_url is called, Then the asset is uploaded to the account's Uploads folder and its asset id is returned.
steps: Call canva_upload_asset_from_url(url=<a publicly reachable PNG/JPEG test image URL>, name="PRD-21299 smoke asset")
expect: canva_get_asset returns the same name and a thumbnail_url; the asset appears in the uploads folder listing
notes: needs a real vendor account; writes a real asset, clean up afterward

text: Given a valid access token, When canva_list_folder_items is called with folder_id omitted (defaults to root), Then it returns the account's top-level designs/folders, paginated the same way as canva_list_designs.
steps: Cross-check a known design/folder from the test account appears in the result
expect: Response contains an items array including the known design/folder, each item with id/type/title-or-name/thumbnail_url, plus a continuation token if the account has more top-level items than the default limit

text: Given two concurrent requests carrying two different tokens, When each calls a Canva tool, Then each outbound call to Canva uses only its own request's token and neither request's context leaks into the other.

Given a mocked Canva transport that returns 429 then 200, When a tool calls it, Then the service retries with backoff and returns the successful result; given a transport that always returns 5xx past the single-call budget, Then it returns a structured upstream_error with retryable true, not a hang or crash.

Given a mocked Canva transport that returns 401 (expired/revoked token), When any tool is called, Then the service returns its own 401/unauthorized immediately, without treating it as a transient/retryable error.

Review round 1 regression: canva_list_designs forwards the clamped `limit` to Canva as a query param (so Canva's own page boundary, and therefore its `continuation` token, matches what is returned), and every item Canva sends within that bound survives to the caller.
evidence: uv run pytest -v on dev/PRD-21299 (post-fix): both tests passed; see Self-test section for the full run.

text: Review round 1 regression: canva_list_folder_items forwards the clamped `limit` to Canva as a query param, same fix and same bug class as canva_list_designs (TC15).
evidence: uv run pytest -v on dev/PRD-21299 (post-fix): test passed; see Self-test section for the full run.
